newsitem.title: USA: CS First Boston cuts Brazil in model portfolio.
newsitem.headline: CS First Boston cuts Brazil in model portfolio.

text.p: CS First Boston analysts Stefano Natella and James Upton decreased the weight of Brazil in their model Latin American stock portfolio Tuesday.
They trimmed Brazil to neutral from overweight, or to 38 percent from 44 percent of the portfolio.
They raised Argentina to overweight from neutral, to 13 percent from 11 percent.
They raised Mexico to slight overweight from neutral, to 32 percent from 29 percent, and raised Venezuela to neutral from underweight, or to 2.5 percent from one percent.

"With Brazil up 31 percent in U.S. dollar terms so far this year -- the best performing market in Latin America -- and most of the good news behind us, we feel that there is room for a pause," Natella and Upton wrote in a report.
"The sale of (state mining company) CVRD (Companhia Vale do Rio Doce) and (power company) Cemig at the end of the month should provide an opportunity to reduce positions on strength.
"... We also believe that over the next two months, Argentina, Mexico and Venezuela will positively surprise investors mainly on the macro front."
